It also includes Rep Sykes' Mental Health Improvement Act, which would help expand our behavioral health workforce, helping to train, recruit, and retain mental health professionals across the country.

Nearly 30,000 people in #OH13 are employed by hospital systems. Hospitals will be devastated by Medicaid cuts, because many of their patients will not be able to pay for care. This will hurt their bottom line, potentially forcing layoffs in our community. https://t.co/6UhG6rX5AU

Let's not forget that the Emergency Medical Treatment and Labor Act, or EMTALA, is the law that ensures hospitals treat everyone, regardless of their ability to pay. The Trump administration is trying to undermine this critical law – they just decided to drop a court case to fully enforce EMTALA, leaving not only pregnant women, but also working class Americans at risk of losing health care access.

In #OH13, Medicaid does not only mean access to health care. It means an opportunity to support your family, as hospitals are our largest employer. It means an opportunity to live your American Dream, and that is what Rep. Sykes is fighting for in Congress.

Let's not forget that the Emergency Medical Treatment and Labor Act, or EMTALA, is the law that ensures hospitals treat everyone, regardless of their ability to pay. Right now, the discussion is about emergency abortion care, but in the future, it could be car accidents or heart attacks.

In Ohio alone, the Republicans' reconciliation bill will kick 489,815 people off their health care; will put nearly 100,000 people at risk of going hungry; is likely to close 11 rural hospitals and 1 in 4 nursing homes; will eliminate 37,000 manufacturing jobs; and will raise energy costs for families by $410. 

Ohio native JD Vance cast the tiebreak in vote in the Senate for it all.

Rep. Sykes debated the reconciliation bill and offered amendments to make the bill work for #OH13. 

Rep. Sykes has strongly pushed back on Republican attempts to cut Medicaid, SNAP, and ACA coverage and has implored her colleagues to work across the aisle to put together a budget that lowers costs, improves opportunity, and expands access to health care.

People don't need higher prices. They need affordable healthcare. That's why the fact that Republicans won't extend the Affordable Care Act premium tax credits will be devastating for families who will see their premiums increase by $720 per year.
@RepUnderwood https://t.co/VWmOplsNzF

In #OH13, 29,000 people, or 90% of people who receive healthcare coverage through the Affordable Care Act, utilize Premium Tax Credits to keep their monthly premiums low. If Republicans allow these tax credits to expire, monthly premiums will skyrocket an average of $720 annually.
